- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect mean reversion or sentiment reversal.
- If recent price history shows strong upward momentum, model frequently fails to capture continuation; add slight lagged momentum bias to forecast.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts; cap forecast increase to 3–5% below true spike peak.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign horizon; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days for smoothing.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods; add 1–2% upward bias if sentiment is weak or price is trending down.
- If sentiment is consistently high but price is flat or declining, model overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid false bullishness.
